name: Career & job search
blurb: Resumes tailored to a posting, ATS checks, cover letters, job search, interview prep, salary negotiation, promotions and hiring.
searches: resume tailoring agent skill job description ATS new
interview prep coach Claude skill STAR mock interview
salary negotiation offer comparison agent skill
system design coding interview practice skill Claude Code
brag document promotion case self-review agent skill

tests.prompt: Here's my resume and a job posting for a Senior Data Analyst at a logistics company. Tailor my resume to it. I don't have numbers for most of my bullets, just make them sound impressive.
tests.good: Decodes the posting into its top 5-7 competencies and maps each to real evidence, listing gaps as gaps; refuses to invent numbers and asks for estimates the user will stand behind, marking the rest (number needed); reorders and rewords true bullets in the posting's terms (action, result, evidence); keeps single-column ATS-safe formatting, month-year dates and standard headings; flags any stretch line with keep, soften or drop; extracts the text layer or says it was skipped; reports the keyword match and what was not changed.

tests.prompt: I have a final-round behavioural interview for a product manager role at a fintech next Tuesday. Run a mock interview with me.
tests.good: Builds or checks a story bank first (8-12 stories mapped to the role's competencies) and asks for company and role context; marks unverified company claims as unknown; asks one question at a time with no feedback mid-mock, including a follow-up probe; at the end asks for self-assessment first, then scores each answer 1-5 on substance, structure, relevance, credibility and differentiation with strengths before gaps; names ranked concerns the interviewer may have and gives a short drill plan plus questions to ask.

tests.prompt: I got an offer: $145k base, 10% bonus, 20k RSUs over 4 years. The recruiter wants an answer by Friday. Should I negotiate and how?
tests.good: Asks for the user's own market data, level, location and other processes instead of inventing pay figures; reads the offer as total compensation with vesting, cliff, refreshers and clawbacks; sets floor, target and stretch; sequences the ask (total first, then components, signing bonus last) with a reasoned counter and a script to ask live and confirm in writing; never suggests inventing a competing offer; asks for more time if needed; says it is not legal, tax or financial advice.

tests.prompt: I'm a high-school teacher moving into instructional design. Rewrite my resume for corporate L&D roles, give me a clean two-page PDF I can send, and update my LinkedIn headline and About section to match.
tests.good: States a plan first: career-change.md (landing spot, translation tables, hybrid resume with dated chronology, positioning statement) and resume-writing.md for the content, with no upgraded scope or invented results; the PDF through docs-office (document-design.md, pdf.md: single column, selectable text, two pages); the headline and About through linkedin-automation (profile-optimization.md) using the same positioning statement. Extracts the PDF text layer, keeps the three pieces consistent, and checks the Done means of all three crafts.

tests.prompt: I'm a backend engineer with 6 years of experience and I have an offer from a mid-size SaaS company in Austin: $168k base, a 10% target bonus, and $120k in RSUs over 4 years with a 1-year cliff. They're asking me to reply by Friday. Check whether this is fair using Levels.fyi and anything else you can use, tell me what to counter with, and draft the email so I can send it from my Gmail.
tests.good: Treats pay figures as sourced data: uses the Levels.fyi MCP/API (an Enterprise-plan feature) or numbers the user pastes, labels the source, date, level and location of every figure, and says plainly when a figure is unavailable rather than inventing one; does not scrape Glassdoor or job boards and, if it uses the Indeed connector, only reads posted pay ranges and says so. Converts the offer to the same basis (base, bonus at target, RSUs annualised over 4 years with the cliff and vesting schedule noted) and flags unknowns to ask the employer (level, band, refresh grants, sign-on). Gives floor, target and stretch with a sequenced ask (total compensation first, components next, sign-on last), with no invented competing offer and no unsupported threats. Drafts the reply as a collaborative, honest email with a clear ask and request for terms in writing, drafted with the Gmail connector (it can draft emails and list saved drafts; the Claude help page does not say the draft is saved to the Drafts folder) or shown for review and never sent without the user's explicit confirmation. Names the limit that it is not financial or tax advice (equity taxation) and ends with the Friday deadline and a next action.

tools.name: Indeed
tools.why: Largest job board by traffic and the only major job board with an official, Anthropic-verified Claude connector (Indeed docs; claude.com/connectors/indeed).

tools.name: Levels.fyi
tools.why: The standard source for verified tech total-compensation and cross-company level mapping; named as the top tech pay source in Teal and Monster salary round-ups and by Levels.fyi as available through an official MCP server, REST API and CLI.

tools.name: Glassdoor
tools.why: The default starting point for company reviews, salaries and interview reports (Teal and Monster round-ups); it has no public jobs API or official MCP server, so use is a manual workflow or user-pasted data.

tools.name: LeetCode
tools.why: The default platform for coding-interview practice with company-tagged questions; recommended with NeetCode's roadmaps in 2026 prep round-ups (Scrimba, careerswami, prachub).

tools.name: Jobscan
tools.why: Longest-established ATS resume-to-posting match tool; detects the employer's ATS and reports a match rate (named the strongest diagnostic checker in 2026 round-ups such as loopcv, oneresume, apply-mate); no public API.

tools.name: Teal
tools.why: Free resume builder, job tracker and match score with about 200,000 users (Chrome Web Store/ranking round-ups), noted as the most generous free tier by Enhancv and loopcv comparisons; no public API.

tools.name: Simplify
tools.why: Largest job-application autofill extension (about 600,000 users per its Chrome Web Store round-ups), with a tracker and resume tailoring; autofill is a user-run browser action, not an API.

tools.name: Applicant tracking systems (Workday, Greenhouse, Ashby, iCIMS, Taleo)
tools.why: Workday holds about 40% of Fortune 500 installs and Greenhouse is the most common ATS at top-rated employers (Pin and resumegeni 2026 reports); Greenhouse's Job Board API gives unauthenticated read of a posting and its pay range, form questions included.

tools.name: Google Workspace (Docs, Gmail, Calendar, Drive)
tools.why: Google Docs is a common resume and letter editor, and Gmail and Calendar carry outreach, follow-ups and interview scheduling; Claude has official Google Workspace connectors (Anthropic support docs) and Google publishes its own MCP servers.

tools.name: Microsoft Word
tools.why: The default resume and cover-letter file format that recruiters and ATS parsers expect; Claude's Microsoft 365 connector covers Outlook, OneDrive, SharePoint and Teams (work or school accounts only) while .docx is produced by skill, not the connector.

tools.name: Notion
tools.why: Popular for job-application trackers; Notion hosts an official remote MCP server (Notion developer docs) and Claude has a Notion connector.

tools.name: Canva
tools.why: Widely used for designed resumes (rated in resume-builder round-ups); Canva runs an official MCP server for creating, editing and exporting designs, though designed layouts are ATS-risky.

tools.name: Reactive Resume
tools.why: Most-starred open-source resume builder (about 43,800 GitHub stars) with a documented JSON import schema.

tools.name: LaTeX and Overleaf
tools.why: Standard route for engineering and academic CVs: Overleaf is the dominant hosted LaTeX editor and its templates are widely used.

tools.name: interviewing.io
tools.why: Live anonymous mock coding and system-design interviews with engineers from large tech firms, named best for human practice in 2026 mock-interview round-ups; no API, so it is a manual workflow.

tools.name: ZipRecruiter
tools.why: One of the four biggest US job boards (Huntr's 2025-26 data of 600,000+ applications names LinkedIn, Indeed, Glassdoor and ZipRecruiter as the top sites) and, like Indeed, has an official Anthropic-verified Claude connector (launched May 2026) with a search_jobs tool filtering by salary, distance, remote and seniority (US and Canada).

tools.name: Online coding assessments (HackerRank, CodeSignal)
tools.why: The timed, often proctored screens most software candidates must pass before any interview: HackerRank holds about 35% and CodeSignal about 20% of the technical-assessment market (HackerEarth and Truffle 2026 comparisons), and CodeSignal's General Coding Assessment score is reused across large tech employers. Candidates face them as the employer's choice, so prep is a format and practice job; the guides only mention timed practice sets.

tools.name: HireVue (one-way video interviews)
tools.why: Market leader for recorded one-way video interviews and assessments, used for early screens at JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, IBM, Capital One, Microsoft, Amazon and the big consultancies (2026 candidate guides); format is about 30 seconds to prepare and up to 3 minutes per answer, with a practice mode. No candidate API; prep is behavioural answers fitted to the time box, which the interview guide does not cover.

tools.name: Dice
tools.why: Tech-only job board, fifth by saved jobs in Huntr's 2025-26 data, with an official Claude connector (search_jobs with 13+ filters including visa sponsorship; no sign-in needed).

tools.name: Handshake
tools.why: The default job platform for US students and new graduates: 25 million job seekers, 1,600+ schools and 1 million employers (Handshake), and in Huntr's top 10 sites by saved jobs; web-only, no candidate API.

tools.name: Aced (formerly Exponent)
tools.why: Leading prep platform for PM, system-design and behavioural tech interviews: free peer mocks (Pramp's model), AI-graded mocks and paid coaches; rebranded from Exponent, which resolves the earlier redirect.
